name: GE Power India Ltd
title: GE Power India Ltd - 532309 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Management is demerging the underutilised Durgapur plant (about INR 27 crores average annual loss, 2023–2025) to JSW Energy, with services order bookings up to INR 734 crores in FY26; no quantified Q1 FY27 numbers given.

utilisation.quote: the facility utilization has become limited largely to the service work and non-coal activities

triggers.label: Durgapur capacity exited via demerger
triggers.quote: the proposed demerger is the right path forward

triggers.label: Core services orders INR 734 crores FY26
triggers.quote: Order bookings have grown from INR 299 crores in 2021-2022 to INR 734 crores in 2025-2026

red_flags.label: Durgapur losses ~INR 27 crores per year
red_flags.quote: this has resulted in an average loss of approximately INR 27 crores per year being booked in GEPIL

red_flags.label: Supply chain dependency on demerged unit
red_flags.quote: A five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy has been put in place

summary.headline: GE Power India proposes demerging its loss-making Durgapur business to JSW Energy; shareholders get 10 JSW Energy shares per 139 GEPIL shares held.
summary.overview: Management presented a two-year turnaround narrative at an investor call held 6 July 2026, covering balance sheet repair, order growth and the proposed demerger. Net worth rose from INR 57 crore (March 2024) to INR 483 crore (March 2026), and cash reached INR 880 crore. The centrepiece was the proposed demerger of the Durgapur undertaking to JSW Energy, which management says has averaged about INR 27 crore annual losses over 2023-2025 due to underutilisation. The call did not include a quarterly financial review or Q&A; no Q1 FY27 numbers were given.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 57 crore in March 2024, more than eight-fold
from a deficit of INR 66 crore in 2023

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by INR 1,364 crore over two years

financial_highlights.change: from loss of INR 251 crore in FY2023
about 34% growth in FY2026; ~25% CAGR since FY2022 from INR 299 crore

segments.name: Core services
segments.commentary: Order bookings rose from INR 299 crore (FY2022) to INR 734 crore (FY2026), about 34% growth in FY2026. Management says the company has frozen commercial strategy and focuses on high-margin, faster-cash-conversion work.

segments.name: Other OEM / third-party fleet
segments.commentary: Order growth rose from about INR 162 crore to about INR 320 crore. Management highlighted expansion into Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Austria, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia and Morocco.

segments.name: Durgapur (proposed demerger)
segments.commentary: Factory and residential township on about 661 acres of leasehold land in West Bengal, making power boiler components, pressure vessels, piping and coal mills. Utilisation has been limited mainly to service and non-coal work since 2023.

guidance_outlook: Demerger to JSW Energy is subject to NCLT sanction; business transfers on a going-concern, as-is-where-is basis, retrospectively effective 1 July 2025.
Share entitlement: 10 fully paid JSW Energy equity shares for every 139 GEPIL shares; GEPIL share count unchanged. Ratio backed by independent valuers and a fairness opinion.
Five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy secures reserved capacity at pre-agreed schedules and pricing.
Management expects full supply chain independence from JSW 'very soon'; no timeline given in numbers.
Board has unanimously approved the scheme; shareholder vote pending.
capex_capacity: Durgapur facility underutilised 2023-2025; service work and non-coal activities only.
Concurrent work to build an independent manufacturing supply chain for core services; no capex amount or timeline disclosed.
Demerger transfers manufacturing, fabrication and capacity at Durgapur to JSW Energy; reserved capacity under five-year agreement.
demand_pricing: Core services order growth of about 34% in FY2026 and ~25% CAGR since FY2022.
Other OEM orders grew to about INR 320 crore from INR 162 crore.
Management says it chases value over volume, prioritising margin and cash conversion; no pricing or realisation figures given.
risks_watch: NCLT sanction and shareholder approval timing for the Durgapur demerger.
Continuity of manufacturing and fabrication support for core services during the transition, given reliance on JSW Energy under the five-year agreement.
Speed of building an independent supply chain; management gave no date.
Whether the core services order momentum (34% FY2026 growth) continues into FY27.
Quarterly Q1 FY27 numbers not yet disclosed in this document.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the turnaround and balance sheet recovery, with repeated emphasis on shareholder value. Less specific on demerger execution details such as supply chain timelines and the Durgapur valuation.
key_quotes: We stopped chasing volume for the sake of revenue and we began chasing the value for the sake of profitability.
Management does not expect any disruption to the manufacturing and fabrication support for the core services business.
the existing number of shares in GEPIL will remain unchanged.

growth.why: No Q1 FY27 numbers or revenue guidance were given; growth is shown historically (core services orders up ~34% in FY26 to INR 734 crore, Other OEM orders up to ~INR 320 crore), and the Durgapur capacity is being exited via a proposed demerger to JSW Energy rather than added.
